sanskrit_verse:
समजातिगुणानां तु वाक्पारुष्ये परस्परम् ।
विनयोऽब्रहितः शास्त्रे पणस्त्वर्धत्रयोदशः ॥५॥
transliteration: samajātiguṇānāṃ tu vākpāruṣye parasparam / vinayo 'bhihitaḥ śāstre paṇastv ardhatrayodaśaḥ // BrhS_1,20.5 //
sph_interpretive_translation: Among equals of same varna and guna, when verbal harshness arises between them, disciplinary correction is prescribed by shastra; but for those of lower capacity, a fine of half-trayodasha is set.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from consciousness capacity, not social position
Causation arises through disruption of harmony via speech
Capacity-based responsibility determines form of corrective action
Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive isolation
Consciousness alignment requires proportional response to distortion
executable_legal_axioms: IF parties are of equal varna AND equal guna AND conflict involves vākpāruṣya THEN apply vinaya protocol
IF party has lower capacity AND vākpāruṣya occurs THEN impose paṇa of ardhatrayodaśa
IF speech causes dissonance in samajāti THEN trigger nyāya review based on pramāṇa alignment
IF corrective action initiated THEN exclude punitive framing and enforce completion process
IF responsibility acknowledged THEN activate consciousness-reintegration pathway
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating disputes among citizens of equivalent status where speech has caused discord, the court shall invoke disciplinary measures aligned with vinaya rather than pecuniary penalties. For cases involving individuals with diminished capacity, a fixed compensatory mechanism applies. The threshold for intervention lies in disruption of societal harmony, not individual offense.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that speech-induced disturbance manifests sequentially: first intention, then utterance, then impact. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures correction aligns with causal depth. Proportional responsibility assigns correction commensurate with awareness level. Non-punitive reality rule mandates restoration of balance without infliction of suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate śabda-saṃskāra completion process to purify speech patterns
Assign responsibility assumption ritual to reaffirm dharma alignment
Implement capacity-enhancement training to prevent recurrence
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma prevails through conscious correction, not punitive reaction. Speech must be purified, not punished. Harmony is restored through capacity-realization, never through suffering. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
